courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Elementary Italian I
courses.description: For students who have no credit in Italian.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Elementary Italian II
courses.description: Continuation of ITAL 101.
courses.prereqText: ITAL 101 or one year of high school Italian.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Exploring Rome: History and Culture of the Eternal City
courses.description: Examines Rome and its roles (religious, political, cultural) in Italian culture from ancient times to the present day. Through history, film, literature, painting and architecture, we will explore the Rome through its various historical and political developments and the effects the city has had on wider Italian and global perception of the "Eternal City". All readings and class meetings are in English.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Freshman Honors Tutorial
courses.description: Study of selected topics on an individually arranged basis. Open only to honors majors or to Cohn Scholars and Associates. May be repeated one time to a maximum of 6 hours.
courses.prereqText: Consent of departmental honors adviser in Italian.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Undergraduate Open Seminar
courses.description: Approved for letter and S/U grading. May be repeated to a maximum of 5 hours.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italian Studies in a Mediterranean Context
courses.description: Introduces students to the study of Italy and Italian culture, emphasizing Italy's central position in Mediterranean networks of cultural, economic and linguistic exchange.
courses.prereqText: ITAL 204 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Intermediate Italian I
courses.description: Continuation of ITAL 102. Introduces students to rapid reading, review of grammar, composition, and conversation.
courses.prereqText: ITAL 102 or two years of high school Italian.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Intermediate Italian II
courses.description: Continuation of ITAL 203. Comprehensive grammar review with emphasis on oral expression and the continued development of reading and written skills.
courses.prereqText: ITAL 103, ITAL 203, or three years of high school Italian.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Practical Review Italian
courses.description: Reviews major challenges in Italian grammar, with particular emphasis on the verb system (major tenses and moods, morphology, and aspect) and areas of contrast with English.
courses.prereqText: Credit or concurrent enrollment in ITAL 204 or equivalent.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Contemporary Italian, Oral and Written
courses.description: Training in oral-aural skill and in writing.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italy Middle Ages & Renaiss
courses.description: The development of Medieval Italian civilization in a literary context from the Sicilian School of love poetry to the early Renaissance in Florence; lectures and readings are in English. Same as CWL 240 and MDVL 240.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Minority Identities in Film and Culture: The Italian American and African American Experience
courses.description: Explores the complex relation between Italian Americans and African Americans in the 19th and 20th century. Were Italian Americans white? What is whiteness? How does identity politics define the relation between minority groups? By looking at the problem of the construction of whiteness among Italian American and at the representation of their relation with African Americans in literature, movies and social studies we will discuss the problem of the relation between two minorities with often conflictual relations in the American context.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Introduction to Italian Cinema
courses.description: Introduction to major films, movements and directors in the Italian tradition, paying particular attention to questions of national identity, gender and political and social history. Knowledge of Italian not required.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Advanced Grammar
courses.description: Study of the structure of modern Italian in both its phonological and syntactic aspects for the student who already has a functional command of the language, with an emphasis on developing ability to analyze and interpret grammatical structures.
courses.prereqText: ITAL 210 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Ital Business & Profess
courses.description: Builds preexisting language skills through the study of Italian business practices: financial systems, transactions, banking, import/export and commercial correspondence.
courses.prereqText: ITAL 210 or equivalent.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Spec Topics Italian Studies
courses.description: Selected substantive readings for independent study on a given special topic of Italian literature, culture, language, or linguistics. May be repeated in separate terms if topics vary up to nine hours.
courses.prereqText: ITAL 204 and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italian Culture and Globalization
courses.description: Introduction to factors that have shaped present-day Italy, with particular attention to globalization; basic concepts contributing to understanding its present social and cultural development in a European and global context. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated in separate terms, if topics vary to a maximum of 6 undergraduate hours and 8 graduate hours.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Dante
courses.description: Interpretation of Dante's Divine Comedy with special attention to its position in the medieval world; a knowledge of Italian not required. Same as CWL 413 and MDVL 413. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Petrarch & Boccaccio
courses.description: Studies in Petrarch and Boccaccio; nonmajors in Italian may read the works in translation; lectures are in English. Same as CWL 414 and MDVL 414. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Fulfillment of campus rhetoric requirement.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Europe and the Mediterranean
courses.description: Examines the governments, societies, and cultures on the shores of the Mediterranean. Examines ideas associated with the Mediterranean and practices followed by its people and governments from the perspectives of a variety of disciplines, paying special attention to the region's relationship with the European Union. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Minimum of junior standing, or consent of instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as EURO 415 and PS 415. See EURO 415.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Language & Minorities in Europe
courses.description: Introduction to political, judicial, linguistic, and cultural issues concerning indigenous and migrant/immigrant languages in the countries of the European Union. Focuses on political and judicial issues, such as legal aspects of bilingual education and minority language use, as well as linguistic and cultural aspects, such as assimilation, language-mixing, and language change. Taught in English. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.pointerText: Same as EURO 418, FR 418, GER 418, LING 418, PS 418, SLAV 418, and SPAN 418. See FR 418.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Masterpieces Renaiss Lit
courses.description: Reading of masterpieces of the 1400 and 1500s and a study of their predecessors and influence; nonconcentrators in Italian may read the works in translation; lectures are in English. Content rotates. Same as CWL 420 and MDVL 420. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours with consent of instructor.
courses.prereqText: Fulfillment of campus rhetoric requirement.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Introduction to Romance Linguistics
courses.description: Comparative and historical analysis of the Romance languages. Instruction in English. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Four semesters of a Romance language or Latin, or equivalent; LING 100, SPAN 252, FR 416, or equivalent; or consent of instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as FR 462, LING 462, PORT 435, RMLG 435 and SPAN 435. See SPAN 435.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Modern Italian Novel
courses.description: An in-depth examination of a particular writer, genre, form or period in modern Italian literature (such as Italo Calvino, Italian detective fiction, or the contemporary Italian novel). See online schedule for specific topic. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: ITAL 200 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italian Syntax & Phonology
courses.description: Introduction to the essential syntactic and phonological structures of Modern Standard Italian in combination with appropriate discussion of corresponding linguistic concepts. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: ITAL 310 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Principles of Language Testing
courses.description: Studies theoretical and practical aspects of language testing. Examines purposes and types of language tests in relation to theories of language use and language teaching goals; discusses testing practices and procedures related to language teaching and language research; and includes the planning, writing, and administration of tests, basic descriptive statistics, and test analysis. A project is required. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: LING 489 or consent of instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as EIL 460, EPSY 487, FR 460, GER 460, PORT 460, and SPAN 460. See EIL 460.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Topics in Italian Cinema
courses.description: An in-depth examination of a particular director, genre or school from the Italian cinematic tradition (e.g., Fellini, Italian horror, or noerealism); topic will very each semester. No knowledge of Italian is required. Same as MACS 470. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated to a maximum of 6 undergraduate hours or 8 graduate hours.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Theoretical Foundations of SLA
courses.description: General introduction to second language acquisition (SLA) theory. Examines nativist, interactionist and cognitive approaches to SLA and explores the role of learner characteristics. Instruction in English. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: An introductory course in linguistics or consent of instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as FR 481, GER 489, LING 489, PORT 489, and SPAN 489. See LING 489.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italian Critical Theory
courses.description: An advanced introduction to the critical theory of major Italian thinkers and philosophers (e.g., Gramsci, Negri, Agamben, Esposito). 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated to a maximum of 6 undergraduate hours or 8 graduate hours if topic varies.
courses.prereqText: At least two 200-level courses in Italian, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Honors Senior Thesis
courses.description: For candidates for honors in Italian. No graduate credit. May be repeated.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Teaching College and Secondary Foreign Language
courses.description: Examination and discussion of classroom goals, procedures and techniques in teaching a foreign language (French, Italian) at the college and secondary level, associated with a demonstration class and supervision of teaching practice. Required of new teaching assistants in the Department of French and Italian.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Seminar in Italian Studies
courses.description: Graduate seminar in Italian culture, literature, linguistics, or critical theory. Topics vary. May be repeated in the same semester to a maximum of 8 hours as topics vary. May be repeated in separate semesters to a maximum of 16 hours as topics vary.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Introduction to Research and Text Criticism
courses.description: Proseminar in literary studies: research and methods; approaches to the literary text. Required of all M.A. and Ph.D. candidates.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Sem Romance Ling
courses.description: Selected topics in comparative Romance linguistics. May be repeated if topics vary.
courses.prereqText: SPAN 435 and consent of instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as FR 559, LING 559, PORT 559, RMLG 559, and SPAN 557. See SPAN 557.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Classroom Language Acquisition
courses.description: Provides for an introduction to the context, process(es), and product of classroom language acquisition; emphasis is placed upon research, research findings, and implications of research.
courses.prereqText: FLTE 471 or equivalent, or consent of instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as EIL 580, FR 580, GER 580, PORT 580, and SPAN 580. See SPAN 580.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Theories in Second Language Acquisition
courses.description: Course introduces doctoral students to current mainstream theories (e.g., linguistic, psycholinguistic, cognitive, and social) used in SLA research. Emphasis is on gaining fundamental understanding of how theories work in SLA, how to evaluate them, and what they attempt to explain.
courses.prereqText: LING 489 or equivalent or consent of instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as CI 584, EALC 584, EPSY 563, FR 584, GER 584, LING 584, PORT 584, and SPAN 584. See SPAN 584.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Sem Second Lang Learn
courses.description: Treats specific topics in second language learning that are of current research and/or theoretical interest. Topics vary from term to term. May be repeated to a maximum of 16 hours if topics vary.
courses.prereqText: SPAN 580 or equivalent or consent of instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as EALC 588, FR 588, GER 588, LING 588, PORT 588, and SPAN 588. See SPAN 588.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Spec Topics in Italian
courses.description: Independent study/research under the direction of a faculty member. May or may not fulfill requirements for a particular degree program in Spanish, Italian, and Portuguese. Consult graduate advisor. May be repeated in same or subsequent terms to a maximum of 8 hours.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated in the same term or in separate terms.
